result_text:
Any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock` now counts as mock resources, whatever follows. The new test passes (3 tests, 0 failures), and the related scoping tests still pass. I did not commit.

**Change** in `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java`: the two mock rules (`__mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+` and `mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+`) are replaced by one rule, `.*/(__)?mock[^/]*/.*`. The `[^/]*` lets the rest of the folder name be anything except a separator, so it covers plain `mock`, punctuation, and non-ASCII. It stays inside one folder segment, so `remock/` and `mock.java`/`mockery.java` files don't match. Backslash paths are handled by the existing normalisation in `SourceFileFilter.pathMatches`. The `mockapi` rule and the other existing rules are unchanged.

**New test** `codeanalyzer/src/test/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/MockResourcesConventionTest.java` covers the three new folder kinds, Windows paths, the previously matched folders (`mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `mock-data/`, `mock_data/`, `mock data/`, `mockStore/`), and the negative cases.
